subject: Materials Science
title: Polymorphism: One Element, Many Structures
description: One-minute skill: Polymorphism: One Element, Many Structures.

hook.text: Carbon makes diamond and graphite — one cuts glass, the other is pencil lead. Same atoms, different crystals.

buildup.text: Polymorphism means a material can adopt different crystal structures depending on conditions.

discovery.text: Iron switches from BCC to FCC at 912°C — this phase transformation enables steel hardening.

twist.text: Tin transforms from metallic to powdery gray tin below 13°C — a plague that crumbled Napoleon's buttons.

climax.text: Zirconia shifts phases with temperature — stabilizing it with yttria makes unbreakable dental crowns.

punchline.text: Change the structure and you change everything — with the same atoms.

quiz.question: What is polymorphism in materials science?
options: A material that can exist in different crystal structures
A material made of many different elements
A crystal that grows in only one direction
